does: Leaves washed rice in cold water until the grains have turned white and plump all through, so that they cook evenly and come out tender in the middle.
how: Put the washed, drained rice in the pot or in a bowl and cover it with cold water.
Leave it until the grains turn from clear to chalky white.
Drain it well and let it sit in the sieve for a short while.
Cook it in fresh measured water.

cues.text: The grains turn from glassy to an even, chalky white.
A grain crushes easily between the fingers, with no hard core.

mistakes.mistake: Soaking for too long in warm weather, so that the rice sours.
mistakes.fix: Soak it in cold water and shorter.

mistakes.mistake: Cooking it in the soaking water, so that the amount of water is wrong.
mistakes.fix: Drain it and add the measured water.

comes_after.why: The rice is soaked after it has been washed.

variant_of.differs: It is a short soak of washed rice in cold water until the grains turn white, and not a long soak of dried pulses, and the water is poured off.
